company.name: Shiftly
company.description: Staff scheduling for shops and restaurants: managers build rotas, staff clock in on their phones, and Shiftly exports hours to payroll. Shops pay for the Pro plan.

title: Shiftly: a month of feedback
brief: Shiftly's inbox for the last 30 days holds 66 pieces of feedback: app reviews, support tickets and NPS comments. The PM who used to triage it has left, and the team plans the next quarter on Monday. Group the feedback into themes, set the noise aside, flag anything critical, rank the themes by what matters, and write opportunities for the top ones.

themes.label: Payroll export loses hours
themes.summary: Since the last release the payroll export drops overtime and split shifts. Staff are underpaid, which is a legal problem for every shop that pays from it.
themes.opportunity: How might we make sure every hour worked reaches payroll, starting with fixing the export and recalculating the affected pay periods?

themes.label: The app crashes
themes.summary: Crashes in core flows. People lose work and cannot finish what they came to do.
themes.opportunity: How might we catch crashes in core flows before release, and fix the top crash signatures this sprint?

themes.label: People cannot log in
themes.summary: Password resets, verification codes and social sign-in fail, and people are locked out of their own data. Every one of these users is fully blocked.
themes.opportunity: How might we make sure nobody stays locked out of Shiftly, with sign-in and recovery that work on the first try?

themes.label: The price feels too high
themes.summary: Complaints about the price and the last increase. Loud and frequent, but people still use the product; it is a positioning question, not a broken experience.
themes.opportunity: How might we make the value of Pro obvious before renewal, so the price feels earned?

themes.label: Getting started is confusing
themes.summary: New users struggle with the first steps. It costs activation quietly: these people rarely complain twice, they just leave.
themes.opportunity: How might we get a new user to publish the schedule in their first two minutes, without a tutorial?

themes.label: Too many notifications
themes.summary: Push and email volume annoys people. Easy to fix and worth fixing, but it does not stop anyone from using the product.
themes.opportunity: How might we let people choose which notifications they get, and send fewer that matter more?

themes.label: Requests for time-off requests
themes.summary: A popular request. It signals what people want next, but its absence does not hurt anyone today.
themes.opportunity: How might we find out which job time-off requests would do for people, and whether a smaller version solves it?

hidden.explanation: The critical problem, "Payroll export loses hours", appears in only 3 items, all from the last 6 days. Few items, but each describes harm that grows every day it stays live, so it goes first whatever the volume. Volume alone would put "The price feels too high" next, with 14 items, but it is a low-severity problem. "The app crashes" (11 items, high severity) and "People cannot log in" (8 items, high severity) hurt more people more. Impact here is reach times severity: low counts 1, medium 2, high 3 per item. 10 items were noise: praise, spam and off-topic messages that belong in no theme.
hidden.principle: Rank feedback by reach times severity, not by volume, and read the rare, recent and severe items first: a critical problem is usually quiet before it gets loud.
